## Correction to this ticket's description — the "burns a round-trip per rung" claim is WRONG

I wrote that line when filing this ticket, carrying it over from the parent's RCA
(`undamaged-adolescent-sable`). The investigation disproved it, and the truth is worse.

**What I wrote:**

> plan-review's size ladder burns a full failed round-trip per rung against an error it cannot
> recognise as terminal-for-this-input.

**What is actually true**, per the RCA comment below: `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` orders
`except LLMUnavailableError: raise` (`:522`) *before* the arm consulting
`is_context_limit_error` (`:524`). Python matches handlers top-to-bottom and
`LLMUnavailableError` IS-A `Exception`, so the earlier arm always wins. **The size ladder is
dead code for the provider signal it was written for.** It does not degrade across rungs — it
burns exactly **one** call and aborts the whole review to an unsigned INDETERMINATE.

So the mis-typing does not merely cost retries; it disables a recovery mechanism entirely and
converts a recoverable oversize input into a failed review.

That was established by a three-way discriminating experiment on identical HEAD code, varying
only the exception type: wrapped -> 1 call and propagates; raw `ModelHTTPError` -> 3 calls and
the ladder engages; an `LLMRunnerError` subclass carrying the same message -> 3 calls and the
ladder engages. That rules out both rival explanations — the message IS recognisable (the
predicate returns `True`), and the ladder is NOT broken (it works the instant the type changes).

Recording this rather than editing the description, because an AC-prose edit would stale the
plan-review attestation. The RCA comment is the authoritative account; where the description
disagrees with it, the RCA wins.

Two other places the record should be read carefully:

- **Attribution differs from the parent's, deliberately.** This is a **regression** traced to
  `fuel-posse-ball` (`96fe-14c6-4c35-4936`, `4e4d055e0f`, 2026-06-25) — one commit introducing
  both the blanket wrap and the guard that hides the ladder from it, two days after the ladder
  shipped. It is NOT the parent's `66b3` omission finding; it was derived independently and the
  divergence is intentional.
- **One surviving mutant is disclosed, not hidden.** M9 (`gate_dispatch` mid-run companion)
  survived; no driver reaches those arms, and the control shows the pre-existing type does not
  reach them either. Filed as `shaggy-crass-bull` (`c72a-48be-054d-4005`), `discovered_from`.
